policy: Original MenubarModelDBus observes the containing chrome document element through its original constructor and removes that observer through its original destructor. Element() remains the actual menubar for existing UI lifecycle.
Original exporter AppendMenuItem handles original XUL key elements, including key/modifier parsing, state and original command activation. No shortcut names, key codes or commands are hardcoded.
The shared D-Bus binding projects key-only metadata into the existing original NSMenu bindings; native fields and global commands therefore see one application menu model.
Native lifecycle menus accept existing key-only entries and preserve them during original branch replacement. Key-only entries cannot be inserted into a popup branch.

Original mutation callbacks and script-runner scheduling refresh the same model after key, keyset and command changes. Original GObject callback sources retain their DOM node until the original callback object retires.
Original NSMenu matching, native key preferences, text editing and Gecko global command cancellation remain unchanged.

The original referenced command element is resolved with nsINode::GetElementById; its live disabled/internal attributes supplement the original key leaf availability. The original exporter only checks the key leaf itself.

Root observation forwards the original menu callbacks only for actual menubar descendants. Original key/keyset/command nodes refresh the registry; unrelated chrome/context-menu mutations do not rebuild the application menu.
